articles.title: दोलखामा दिनभर धार्मिक परिक्रमा, रातभर लाखे नाच !
articles.summary:
दोलखा । प्राचीन तथा ऐतिहासिक नगरी दोलखामा धार्मिक सहिष्णुता र सांस्कृतिक सद्भावको प्रतीक मानिने परम्परागत हिले जात्रा अर्थात् गुउँला पर्व हर्षोल्लासका साथ मनाइँदैछ । श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदा अर्थात् घण्टाकर्ण (गाठामा) को तेस्रो दिनदेखि सुरु भएको यो ऐतिहासिक पर्वका कारण यतिबेला दोलखा बजार २४ सै घण्टा सांस्कृतिक रौनकमा झुमिरहेको छ ।

बिहानैदेखि गुञ्जने परम्परागत बाजा, धार्मिक परिक्रमा र दिउँसोदेखि रातिसम्म देखाइने फरक स्वरूपका लाखे नाचले प्राचीन नगरी दोलखा यतिबेला गुञ्जायमान बनेको छ । घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् स्थानीय भाषामा ‘गाठामा’को तेस्रो दिन, श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदादेखि दोलखामा गुउँला जात्राको औपचारिक सुरुवात हुन्छ ।

माथिल्लो र तल्लो टोलका बेग्लाबेग्लै डापा खलक परम्परागत बाजागाजासहित बिहानै सांस्कृतिक परिक्रमामा निस्कन्छन् । स्थानीय भाषामा देउ उय भनिने यो परिक्रमा कागे अष्टमीका दिन समापन हुन्छ ।

पूजा सामग्री बोकेका ज्येष्ठ नागरिकसहितको टोली स्वयंभू चैत्य र कोर्छे टोलबाट सुरु भई भीमेश्वर, कालीमन्दिर, त्रिपुरा सुन्दरी, राजकुलेश्वर तलेजु, नक्छे चैत्य, गणेश मन्दिर र मच्चिछन्द्रनाथ मन्दिर हुँदै पुनः स्वयंभू चैत्य पुगेर टुंगिन्छ । जात्रा मनाउँदा हिन्दू र बौद्ध दुवै धार्मिकस्थलको समान रूपमा परिक्रमा गरिन्छ ।

दिउँसोदेखि दोलखा बजारमा लाखे नाचको रौनक सुरु हुन्छ । एउटै जात्रामा चार फरक स्वरूपका लाखे प्रदर्शन हुने भएकाले दोलखाको लाखे देशभरमै विशेष मानिन्छ ।

दिउँसो ३ देखि ५ बजेसम्म ‘जोङ डाकस’ निकालिन्छ । यसमा हात दुई जना दाउरेले समातेर दर्शकलाई लखेट्दै मनोरञ्जन गराउँछन् । आसुरी शक्तिमाथि विजयको कथा भन्ने नेपाल डाकस भने राति मात्र नाचिन्छ । वर्षमा एक दिन रक्षाबन्धनका दिन निकालिने ‘ड्वाकु डाकस’ ठूलो लाखे हो । फरक मुखुण्डो लगाइने यसलाई महाकालीका रूपमा पूजा गरिन्छ ।

गाईजात्रादेखि पञ्चमीसम्म ‘माझीपा डाकस’ पनि प्रदर्शन गरिन्छ । डोरीले बाँधेर लाखेलाई नचाउने र माझीहरूले नियन्त्रण गर्न खोजेको लोककथाको अभिनय यसमा देखाइन्छ । पुस्तौँदेखि चल्दै आएको यस अमूर्त कला र संस्कृति संरक्षणमा स्थानीय युवाको सक्रियता उदाहरणीय छ ।

articles.title: माननीयको अभिब्यक्तिले सुरक्षा संगठनको बदनाम
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । मुलुकको शान्ति, सुरक्षा र कानुन कार्यान्वयनको मुख्य जिम्मेवारी बोकेको नेपाल प्रहरी अहिले दोहोरो दबाबमा परेको छ । एकातिर गत बर्षको भदौ २३ र २४ गतेको आन्दोलनका क्रममा संगठनले भोगेको भौतिक तथा मनोवैज्ञानिक क्षतिको असर अझै पूर्णरूपमा मेटिन सकेको छैन भने, अर्कोतिर राजनीतिक वृत्तबाटै संगठनको नेतृत्व र कार्यशैलीमाथि प्रश्न उठाउने क्रम तीव्र बनेको छ ।

राज्यकै प्रमुख निकायहरु कार्यपालिका र ब्यवस्थापिकाबाटै प्रहरी संगठनको बदनाम गर्ने कार्यले संगठनको मनोबल झनै गिराएको छ । सार्वजनिक पदमा बसेका व्यक्तिले उठाउने प्रश्नले सधैं सार्वजनिक चासो निम्त्याउँछ, विशेषगरी त्यो प्रश्न राज्यको कुनै संवेदनशील निकायविरुद्ध उठाइएको हुँदा गत बुधबार सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिको बैठकमा रास्वपाका सांसद खगेन्द्र सुनारले नेपाल प्रहरीको सामग्री खरिद प्रक्रियामा प्रश्न उठाउँदै प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्कीलाई नै कठघरामा उभ्याए ।

जुत्ता, मोजा, पोशाकदेखि लाठी खरिदसम्ममा आर्थिक अनियमितता भएको आशय दिँदै उनले तत्काल निष्पक्ष छानबिनको माग गरे । आइजीपी कार्कीले तत्काल प्रतिवाद गरे । खरिद प्रक्रियामा कुनै अनियमितता नभएको दाबी गर्दै तथ्यहीन आरोप लगाएर कर्मचारीको मनोबल कमजोर नबनाउन आग्रह गरे ।

त्यसपछि सांसद सुनारकै आफ्नै कानुनी पृष्ठभूमिबारे सार्वजनिक बहस सुरु भयो — प्रश्न उठाउने व्यक्ति स्वयं कति चोखो छ ? आईजीपी कार्कीले सांसद सुनारविरुद्ध नै आएका उजुरीहरूको चाङ औंल्याए । सुनारविरुद्ध माननीयदेखि दयनीयसम्मका व्यक्तिहरूले विभिन्न प्रकृतिका उजुरी दिएको र, आरोपको पोको खोलिदिन सक्ने चेतावनी दिए ।

सर्वत्र आलोचित खगेन्द्र अझै ‘अराजक’

लेखा समितिमा आईजीपी कार्कीमाथि खगेन्द्र सुनारले उठाएको प्रश्नले मात्रै खगेन्द्र चर्चा र विवादमा आएका होइनन् । प्रहरी संगठन विरुद्ध पटक पटक सार्वजनिक उनको अभिब्यक्तिले सांसद सुनार आलोचित छन् ।

२०८३ वैशाख ७ गते सिन्धुली सुनकोशी गाउँपालिका–३ जुम्लीडाँडा निवासी २३ वर्षीय श्रीकृष्ण विक खुर्कोटस्थित प्रहरीको हिरासतमै मृत्यु भएको घटनामा जनप्रतिनिधिको हैसियतमा सिन्धुली पुगेका सुनाले एकतर्फी आरोप लगाउँदै सिन्धुलीका एसपीको कठालो नै समातेर घिसार्नुपर्ने अभिव्यक्ति दिएका थिए ।

सांसद हुनुपूर्व सुनारले एक वर्षअघि माइतीघरबाट समेत जिल्ला प्रहरी परिसर काठमाडौंका एकजना डीएसपी विरुद्ध अर्मयादित अभिव्यक्ति दिएका थिए । त्यो बेला जहाँ पनि उनी हातमा नेल र निधारमा नवसेना लेखिएको फेटा बाँधेर सांकेतिक विरोधमा देखिन्थे । यो पटक संसदीय समितिमा आईजीपी कार्कीविरुद्ध पनि उही शैलीमा आक्रोश पोखेका थिए ।

सुनारविरुद्ध तीन मुद्दा अदालतमा विचाराधिन

सांसद खगेन्द्र माथि अहिले पनि तीनवटा मुद्दा अदालतमै विचाराधीन छ । दैलेखको नारायण नगरपालिका–२ भैसेखोरका खगेन्द्र प्रतिनिधि सभाको चुनावमा भने बाँके क्षेत्र नम्बर ३ बाट निर्वाचित भएका हुन् । उनीमाथि सुर्खेत प्रहरीले २०८० को असारमा पक्राउ गरेर सार्वजनिक शान्तिविरुद्धको कसुरमा मुद्दा चलाएको थियो ।

त्यो बेला जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय सुर्खेतले २० हजार रुपैयाँ धरौटी लिएर छाडेको थियो । त्यसको एक वर्षपछि पुनः २०८१ असारमै सुर्खेतकै अस्पतालका डाक्टरहरुमाथि अभद्र व्यवहार तथा तोडफोडको मुद्दा हाल सुर्खेत जिल्ला अदालतमा विचाराधीन अवस्थामा छ । २०८२ साउनमा काभ्रेकी एक महिलामाथि सामाजिक सञ्जाल फेसबुकमार्फत चरित्र हत्या गर्ने खालको पोष्ट गरेको आरोपमा उनीमाथि काभ्रे प्रहरीले साइबर अपराधमा मुद्दा चलाएको थियो ।

साउन ५ गते पक्राउ पुर्जी लिए पनि उनी पक्राउ भने परेनन् । पछि मुद्दा अदालत दर्ता भएपछि उनी काभ्रे जिल्ला अदालतमा हाजिर भएका थिए । काभ्रे अदालतले समेत सुनारलाई ५० हजार रुपैयाँ धरौटी बुझाएर मात्रै छाड्ने आदेश गरेका थिए । हालसम्म पनि मुद्दा टुंगो लागेको छैन ।

सुनारको प्रहरी नेतृत्वमाथि भएको व्यक्तिगत आक्षेप र अमर्यादित व्यवहार विवाद गृहमन्त्री हुँदै सभामुखसम्म पुगेको छ । आइजिपीसहित आठ एआइजी र एक डिआइजीले प्रहरी संगठनकै मनोबल खस्किएको भन्दै संसदीय छानबिनमा विधि र मर्यादा पालना गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन् ।

बेनामे उजुरीको भरमा संसदीय समितिमा बोलाएर संगठनकै मानमर्दन हुने गरी हुर्मत लिएको गुनासो समेत गरेका छन् । प्रहरी अधिकारी मात्र होइन, गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङसमेत सुनारको ब्यवहारले रुष्ट छन् ।

प्रहरी संगठनबाटै ‘माननीय’विरुद्ध खेद ब्यक्त

प्रतिनिधिसभा सदस्य सुनारको अराजक अभिब्यक्तिको सिंगो प्रहरी संगठनले नै खेद प्रकट गरेको छ । नेपाल प्रहरी पूर्वप्रहरी संगठन प्रमुख मञ्चले विज्ञप्ति जारी गरेर सुरक्षा निकाय र यसको नेतृत्वमाथि भएका व्यक्तिलक्षित टीकाटिप्पणीप्रति खेद प्रकट गरेको छ ।

भने पूर्वप्रहरी कर्मचारी परिषद्, पूर्वसशस्त्र प्रहरी संघ र सुरक्षा तथा न्याय अध्ययन केन्द्रले संयुक्त विज्ञप्ति जारी गरेर यस्ता गतिविधिले सुरक्षाकर्मीको मनोबल खस्कने र राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षामै असर पर्ने स्पष्ट गरेका छन् । साथै ती संस्थाहरूले संसदीय समितिमा बोलाउँदा पदीय गरिमा, सम्मान र व्यावसायिक मर्यादा कायम राख्न सुझाएका छन् ।

अझै पुरिएको छैन भदौ २४ को घाउ

नेपाल प्रहरीका लागि २०८२ भदौ २३ र २४ गते घटनाको घाउ अझै पुरिएको छैन । त्यो घटनाले संगठनको भौतिक संरचना, हतियार, कार्यालय र प्रहरी कर्मचारीको सुरक्षामाथि नै ठूलो चुनौती खडा गरेको छ ।

उक्त आन्दोलनका क्रममा काठमाडौँ उपत्यकाका मात्र १ सय ५३ प्रहरी कार्यालयमा आगजनी, १७ वटा प्रहरी वृत्त क्षतिग्रस्त,१ हजार १ सय हतियार लुटिपाट,३ जना प्रहरीको मृत्यु र प्रहरी कर्मचारीले ज्यान जोगाउन बर्दी फुकालेर भाग्नुपर्ने अवस्था आएको थियो ।

सुरक्षा संगठन र कर्मचारीको मनोबल बढाउनुपर्नेमा सत्तारुढ दलबाट नै यस्ता खाले अभिव्यक्तिले संगठनको मनोबल गिर्दो अवस्थामा पुगेको पूर्व प्रहरी अधिकारीको भनाई छ ।

सांसदको काम प्रश्न उठाउनु नै हो, तर प्रश्न उठाउने नाममा प्रमाणविनाका आरोप लगाउनु र आरोप प्रमाणित नहुँदै त्यसलाई सत्यका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गर्नु जिम्मेवार राजनीतिक अभ्यास होइन । खगेन्द्र सुनार हिजो आन्दोलनकारी भए पनि आज जनताका प्रतिनिधि हुन् ।

त्यसैले विना आधार राज्यको जिम्मावार निकायहरुको बदनाम गर्दा सुरक्षा संगठनको मात्र होइन, स्वयम् माननीयको ओज घटाउँछ । प्रहरीलाई प्रश्न गरौँ, तर प्रमाणसहित ।

प्रहरीलाई जवाफदेही बनाऔँ, तर संस्थागत रूपमा । प्रहरी कमजोर हुँदा कमजोर हुने प्रहरी प्रमुख मात्र होइन, सिंगो राज्य हो । प्रहरी संगठनका भित्रका कमजोरीहरु सुधार हुनु पर्छ नै, सांसद सुनारको आफू पनि सुध्रिन जरुरी छ ।

articles.title: पूर्वी नाकाबाट विदेशी पर्यटक बढे, सबैभन्दा धेरै भुटानी
articles.summary:
झापा । पूर्वी नेपालको प्रमुख स्थलमार्ग काँकरभिट्टा नाका हुँदै आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\८३ मा ८६ देशका ९ हजार ४४७ जना विदेशी पर्यटक नेपाल भित्रिएका छन्। अध्यागमन कार्यालय काँकरभिट्टाको तथ्याङ्कअनुसार यो संख्या दैनिक औसत करिब २६ जना विदेशी पर्यटक नेपाल प्रवेश गरेको हो ।

आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\८३ मा काँकरभिट्टा नाकाबाट नेपाल प्रवेश गर्ने विदेशी पर्यटकमा भुटान, अमेरिका, थाइल्याण्ड, अष्ट्रेलिया, बेलायत, क्यानडा, जर्मनी, फ्रान्स, जापान र रुसलगायत देशका नागरिक छन् । कुल आगन्तुकमध्ये भुटानी नागरिकको हिस्सा सबैभन्दा ठूलो छ । ४ हजार ९९४ जना भुटानी नागरिक नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् ।

जुन कुल पर्यटक संख्याको करिब ५३ प्रतिशत हो । त्यस्तै २ हजार १५२ जना अमेरिकी नागरिकले काँकरभिट्टा नाका हुँदै नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् । यो कुल आगन्तुकको करिब २३ प्रतिशत हो । भारतका नागरिकलाई नेपाल प्रवेश गर्न भिसा आवश्यक नपर्ने भएकाले उनीहरूलाई तेस्रो मुलुकका पर्यटकसम्बन्धी तथ्याङ्कमा समावेश गरिएको छैन ।

महिनागत तथ्याङ्कअनुसार सबैभन्दा बढी विदेशी पर्यटक पुसमा १ हजार ८५० जना र सबैभन्दा कम भदौमा २१६ जना नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् । अध्यागमन कार्यालयले पुस र माघलाई प्रमुख पर्यटकीय याम मानेको छ ।

पर्यटकको आगमन उत्साहजनक भएपनि बसाइ छोटो हुने गरेको होटल व्यवसायी बताउँछन। पूर्वी नेपालका पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यमा पर्यटकलाई केही दिन रोक्न सके झापा, इलाम, ताप्लेजुङलगायत जिल्लाको पर्यटन तथा होटल व्यवसायमा उल्लेख्य योगदान पुग्ने उनीहरूको भनाइ छ ।

पूर्वी नेपालका पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यको अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रचारप्रसार र सीमा नाकामै यातायात, होटल तथा भ्रमणसम्बन्धी सूचना उपलब्ध गराउनुपर्ने पर्यटन व्यवसायी कुन्दन निरौला बताउँछन् ।

अध्यागमन कार्यालय काँकरभिट्टाले सन् २०२४ अगस्टदेखि पूर्ण रूपमा अध्यागमन सेवा सञ्चालन गरेको थियो । सेवा प्रभावकारी भएपछि विदेशी पर्यटकको आगमन क्रमशः बढेको सूचना अधिकारी इन्द्रकुमार राजवंशी बताउँछन् ।

अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रचारप्रसार, पर्यटन सूचना केन्द्र र आकर्षक प्याकेज निर्माणसँगै संघ, प्रदेश र स्थानीय तहबीच समन्वय गर्न सके विदेशी पर्यटकको संख्या बढाउन सकिने देखिन्छ । यसबाट होटल, यातायात, ट्राभल्स, हस्तकला तथा स्थानीय उत्पादनको बजारसमेत लाभान्वित हुने देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: राँगाको सिङबाट बन्ने गुँला पर्वको मुख्य बाजा !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेवार समुदायका विशेषगरी बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीको प्रमुख सांस्कृतिक पर्व गुँला बिहीबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ । एक महिनासम्म मनाइने पर्वमा भक्तजनले परम्परागत बाजागाजासहित चैत्य, विहार र मन्दिरको परिक्रमा गर्दै बुद्धको पूजा–आराधना गर्ने गर्दछन् ।

काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका परम्परागत नेवार वस्ती र टोलहरुमा अब एक महिनासम्म सडक वा गल्लीहरुमा विहान मानिसहरुको चहलपहल शुरु नहुँदै सुनिने छ, धिमे, भुस्या, बाँसुरी र न्याकुँको सुमधुर आवाज । अनि बाजाको यही धुन पछ्याउँदै मानिसहरू चैत्यतर्फ अघि बढिरहेका हुने छन् । यो गुँला पर्वको अवसरमा देखिने दृश्य हो ।

नेवार समुदायमा पनि विशेषगरी बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीले मनाउने गुँला पर्व बिहीबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ । श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदादेखि भाद्र शुक्ल प्रतिपदासम्म चल्ने यो पर्व करिब एक महिनासम्म धार्मिक र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकालाई जीवन्त बनाउँछ ।

गुँला शब्दको अर्थ आफैमा रोचक पनि छ । नेपाल भाषामा ‘गुँ’ को अर्थ नौ र ‘ला’ को अर्थ महिना भन्ने गरिन्छ । नेपाल संवतको नवौँ महिनामा मनाइने भएकाले यसको नाम गुँला रहन गएको मानिन्छ । गुँलाको वास्तविक आकर्षण बिहानै सुरु हुने यात्रामा देखिन्छ । भक्तजनहरू परम्परागत बाजा बजाउँदै विभिन्न चैत्य, विहार, बहाः र बहीको परिक्रमा गर्छन् ।

काठमाडौंको स्वयम्भू, बौद्ध, पाटनलगायतका धार्मिक तथा ऐतिहासिक स्थलमा गुँला पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखिन्छ । एउटा समूह धिमे बजाउँदै अघि बढिरहेको हुन्छ । यसमा कसैले भुस्या बजाइरहेको हुन्छ भने कसैले न्याकुँको गहिरो आवाज निकालिरहेको हुन्छ । यही दृश्यले गुँलालाई काठमाडौँका अन्य धेरै जात्रा र पर्वहरुभन्दा फरक बनाएको छ ।

गुँला पूजा र परिक्रमा गर्ने पर्व मात्रै होइन । संगीत जोडिएको उपत्यकाको जीवित संस्कृति पनि हो । विशेषगरी न्याकुँ बाजा गुँलाको पहिचानसँग जोडिएको छ । राँगाको सिङबाट बनाइने यो बाजा हेर्दा साधारण देखिए पनि यसको ध्वनि निकै विशिष्ट हुन्छ ।

परम्परागत रूपमा धार्मिक यात्राहरुमा यसको प्रयोग हुँदै आएको छ । त्यसैगरी धिमे, बाँसुरी, भुस्या र धाः लगायतका बाजासँगै बज्दा यी आवाजले पनि गुँला पर्वमा सांगीतिक समूहको स्वरूप लिन्छन् । पछिल्लो समय यस्ता जात्रा पर्वमा नयाँ पुस्ताको सहभागिता पनि बढिरहेको छ । नयाँ पूस्ताको सहभागितासँगै परम्परागत पर्व र संस्कृति पुस्तान्तरण पनि हुँदैछन् ।

गुँला धार्मिक पर्व मात्रैमा सीमित छैन । सामाजिकरुपमा खेतीपातीको मुख्य काम सकिएको समयसँग पनि यो पर्व जोडिएको छ । मानिसहरू केही फुर्सदिला हुने यही समयमा समुदाय भेला हुने, भेटघाट गर्ने र सामूहिक रूपमा धार्मिक गतिविधिमा सहभागी हुने अवसर पनि गुँलाले जुटाइ दिएको छ ।

बौद्ध परम्परामा वर्षायामको साधना र धार्मिक अभ्याससँग पनि गुँला समयको सम्बन्ध जोडिन्छ । त्यसैले यो अवधि पूजा, ध्यान, पाठ, दान र पुण्यकर्मका लागि विशेष मानिन्छ । यसको अर्को पक्ष के भने गुँला पर्वमा हुने चैत्य परिक्रमा एउटा यात्रा मात्रै होइन ।

उपत्यकाका विभिन्न स्थानीय धार्मिक स्थललाई जोड्ने सांस्कृतिक नेटवर्क जस्तो पनि हो । एउटा टोलबाट अर्को टोल, एउटा बहाःबाट अर्को चैत्यसम्म बाजाको धुनले यी ठाउँहरूलाई जोडिरहेको हुन्छ । काठमाडौंलाई मन्दिरै–मन्दिरको सहर भनिन्छ । तर गुँला पर्वले कामठाडौँ बाजा, बहाः, बही र चैत्यहरूको पनि सहर हो भन्ने प्रमाण पनि दिन्छ । एक महिनासम्म बज्ने यी बाजाहरु पुर्खाको स्मृति हुन्, धार्मिक आस्था हुन् र पहिचानको आवाज हुन् ।

articles.title: काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णयकाे एनआरएनएद्वारा स्वागत
articles.summary:
काठमाडाैँ । काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेपछि गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) पोर्चुगलले उक्त निर्णयको स्वागत गर्दै नेपाल तथा पोर्चुगल सरकारप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरेको छ।

नेपाल सरकारको २०८३ साउन २६ गते बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले पोर्चुगल सरकारलाई काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय खोल्न सहमति दिने निर्णय गरेको थियो। निकट भविष्यमा नै कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आउने अपेक्षा गरिएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलका अध्यक्ष सुजन लामा मोक्तानले जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिमा काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीलाई विभिन्न कन्सुलर सेवा लिन सहज हुने उल्लेख गरिएको छ। विशेषगरी पारिवारिक पुनर्मिलन, भिसा तथा अन्य कन्सुलर सेवाका लागि हाल भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने बाध्यता कम हुने संघको विश्वास छ।

नयाँ सरकार गठन भएपछि काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनाका लागि नेपाल सरकारको तर्फबाट आवश्यक पहल अघि बढाइएको थियो। सोही क्रममा परराष्ट्रमन्त्री शिशिर खनालले पोर्चुगलका राज्य तथा विदेश मामिलामन्त्री पाउलो राङ्गेलसँग टेलिफोन संवाद गरी कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनालगायतका विषयमा कुराकानी गरेका थिए।

नेपाल सरकारको अनुरोध तथा त्यसपछिका कूटनीतिक पहलपछि पोर्चुगल सरकारले काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेको हो। एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले यसलाई पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपाली समुदायका लागि महत्वपूर्ण उपलब्धिका रूपमा लिएको छ।

नेपाल र पोर्चुगलबीच १ सेप्टेम्बर १९७६ मा औपचारिक कूटनीतिक सम्बन्ध स्थापना भएको थियो। लामो समयसम्म नेपालले पोर्चुगलमा आवासीय दूतावास स्थापना नगरेका कारण पोर्चुगलसम्बन्धी नेपाली कूटनीतिक जिम्मेवारी पेरिसस्थित नेपाली दूतावासले सम्हाल्दै आएको थियो।

नेपाल सरकारले सन् २०२५ मार्चमा लिस्बनमा आवासीय नेपाली राजदूतावास स्थापना गरेको थियो। लिस्बनमा स्थापना भएको नेपाली दूतावासका पहिलो आवासीय राजदूत प्रकाशमणि पौडेल हुन्।

दूतावासको औपचारिक उद्घाटन भने २० फेब्रुअरी २०२६ मा परराष्ट्र सचिव अमृतबहादुर रायको पोर्चुगल भ्रमणका क्रममा गरिएको थियो। यससँगै नेपाल–पोर्चुगल सम्बन्ध थप संस्थागत र प्रत्यक्ष बनेको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलको भनाइ छ।

पोर्चुगलमा नेपालीको यकिन तथ्यांक नभए पनि ६० हजारभन्दा बढी नेपाली रहेको अनुमान नेपाली दूतावासले गरेको छ। ठूलो संख्यामा नेपाली समुदाय रहेको पोर्चुगलका लागि काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर सेवा सुरु हुनु महत्वपूर्ण कदम भएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीले सेवा लिन भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने अवस्थाको अन्त्य हुने तथा समय र आर्थिक खर्चसमेत बचत हुने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थको संयुक्त आयोजनामा गरिएको तारकेश्वर–६ स्थित महांकाल मन्दिर क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

बुधबार बिहान ७ः३० बजेदेखि सञ्चालन गरिएको कार्यक्रममा ३५ जना रोटेरियन तथा रोट्रयाक्ट सदस्यहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो। सहभागीहरूले मन्दिर परिसर तथा आसपासका क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ गर्दै फोहोर व्यवस्थापन र स्वच्छ वातावरण निर्माणसम्बन्धी जनचेतना फैलाएका छन् ।

कार्यक्रमले सार्वजनिक स्थलको स्वच्छता कायम राख्नुका साथै युवाहरूलाई सामाजिक सेवामा सक्रिय रूपमा सहभागी गराउने उद्देश्य राखेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

रोटरीको Create Lasting Impact भन्ने मूल भावनाअनुसार आयोजित कार्यक्रममा सहभागीहरूले समुदायको विकास र वातावरण संरक्षणका लागि यस्ता सामाजिक अभियानलाई निरन्तरता दिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिएका छन् ।

रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थले आगामी दिनमा पनि समुदाय केन्द्रित विभिन्न सामाजिक तथा वातावरणीय कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सद्वारा कर्णालीकी छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले कर्णाली प्रदेशबाट काठमाडौं आई जोरपाटीस्थित चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालय कक्षा १२ मा अध्ययनरत छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको छ । शिक्षाको माध्यमबाट विद्यार्थीको क्षमता विकास तथा उज्ज्वल भविष्य निर्माणमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा शीता शाहीलाई छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको हो । आफ्नो जन्मस्थान कर्णाली प्रदेश भए पनि काठमाडौंमा रही अध्ययन गर्दै आएकी शीता शाहीलाई प्रदान गरिएको यस सहयोगले उनको शैक्षिक यात्रालाई थप सहज बनाउँदै उच्च शिक्षा तथा आगामी लक्ष्यतर्फ अघि बढ्न प्रेरणा प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास फाइनान्सले लिएको छ ।

छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गर्दै आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई उज्ज्वल भविष्यका लागि हार्दिक बधाई तथा शुभकामना व्यक्त गरेको छ । साथै, आगामी दिनमा पनि अध्ययनमा निरन्तर मेहनत, लगनशीलता र समर्पणका साथ अघि बढ्दै उत्कृष्ट सफलता हासिल गर्न प्रोत्साहित गरेको छ ।

उक्त छात्रवृत्ति वितरण कार्यक्रमा आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सका प्रबन्धक अच्युत पण्डित, बौद्ध शाखा प्रबन्धक अजय राज रेग्मी, बजार व्यवस्थापन प्रमुख सञ्जोक गुरुङ तथा बजार व्यवस्थापन अधिकृत सरिना श्रेष्ठ लगायत चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालयका प्रधानाध्यापक तथा शिक्षकहरू र सामाजिक अभियान्ता टेक राज शाहीको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको थियो।

आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत शिक्षा क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै आर्थिक तथा सामाजिक रूपमा सहयोगको आवश्यकता भएका विद्यार्थीको शैक्षिक विकासमा योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ। कम्पनीले आगामी दिनमा पनि शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य तथा अन्य सामाजिक क्षेत्रमा आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्वलाई निरन्तरता दिने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

articles.title: भृकुटीमण्डपमा नयाँ गाडी र बाइकको मेला, इभीमा सबैको आकर्षण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डपमा मंगलबारदेखि नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ सुरु भएको छ । ५५ वटा ब्रान्ड सहभागी यो एक्स्पोमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन प्रदर्शन गरिएका छन् ।

अटोप्रेमीहरूका लागि नयाँ गाडी खरिद गर्ने र नयाँ अपडेट बुझ्ने अवसर एक्स्पोले जुराएको छ । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डप अहिले नयाँ मोडलका गाडी, मोटरसाइकल र अत्याधुनिक मोबिलिटी प्रविधिले भरिएको छ । र, यो माहोलको अवसर नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ ले जुटाएको हो । नेपाल अटोमोबाइल इम्पोर्टर्स एण्ड म्यानुफ्याक्चरर्स एशोसिएसन अर्थात् नाइमाले दोस्रोपटक आयोजना गरेको एक्स्पो मंगलबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ ।

नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्की र नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतुसिंह वैद्यले पानसमा बत्ती बालेर एक्स्पोको औपचारिक शुभारम्भ गरे । यसपटकको एक्स्पोमा ५५ वटा ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् । जसमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन सार्वजनिक तथा प्रदर्शन गरिँदैछन् ।

नयाँ गाडी वा बाइक किन्ने सोचमा रहेकाहरुलाई भृकुटीमण्डपमा जारी एक्स्पो उत्कृष्ट गन्तव्य हुन सक्छ । एक्स्पोमा चारपांग्रेतर्फ हुन्डाई, टाटा, टोयोटा, महिन्द्रा, किया, निसान, बीवाईडी, एमजी, सिट्रोन, ओमोडा एन्ड जेको, डेन्जा, जिकर, लीपमोटर, वुलिङ, ग्रेट वाल मोटर्सलगायतका ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् ।

त्यसैगरी दुईपांग्रेतर्फ बजाज, होन्डा, टीभीएस, रोयल इन्फिल्ड, केटीएम, सुजुकी, एथर, याडिया, अल्ट्राभायोलेट, सीएफ मोटो, ट्रायम्फलगायतका ब्राण्डले आफ्ना नयाँ उत्पादन प्रदर्शनीमा राखेका छन् ।

कमर्सियल भेहिकलतर्फ पनि चेरी वान्डा, केरी, डोङफेङ, स्काइवर्थलगायतका ब्राण्डका गाडीहरु एक्स्पोमा देख्न सकिन्छ । एक्स्पोको अर्को आकर्षणमा रुपमा यहाँ रहेका स्टलहरु र छुट अफर रहेको छ । ग्राहकलाई आकर्षित गर्न कम्पनीहरूले आकर्षक तथा फरक शैलीका स्टल निर्माण गरेका छन् । विभिन्न ब्राण्डले विशेष छुट र अफरसमेत सार्वजनिक गरिरहेका छन् ।

नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतु सिंह वैद्यका अनुसार नेपालको अटोमोबाइल क्षेत्र विस्तारै विद्युतीय सवारीतर्फ अघि बढिरहेको छ । विद्युतीय सवारीले हरित अर्थतन्त्र निर्माणमा योगदान पु¥याइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले नेपालमा अटो कम्पोनेन्ट उद्योगलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्न सके एसेम्बल प्लान्टको सम्भावना अझ बलियो हुने बताएकी छन् ।

एक्स्पोमा सवारीसाधनसँगै बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्था र बीमा कम्पनीको सहभागिता छ भने विभिन्न नलेज सिरिज पनि सञ्चालन भइरहेका छन् । नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो साउन ३१ गतेसम्म सञ्चालन हुनेछ ।

articles.title: घण्टाकर्णका आतंक र अन्त्यको कथा गथाँमुगः पर्व
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायले मंगलवार घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाएका छन् । घण्टाकर्ण दानवको अन्त्य गरिएको स्मरणमा मनाइने यो पर्वमा तीनखुट्टे राक्षसको आकृति बनाएर साँझ आगोमा जलाउँदै भूतप्रेत, रोगव्याधि र नकारात्मक शक्ति भगाउने परम्परा छ । गथाँमुगःको अवसरमा काठमाडौं, भक्तपुर र ललितपुरमा यो पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखियो ।

प्रत्येक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौंका गल्ली, चोक र दोबाटोमा नरकट, छ्वाली र काठबाट एउटा अनौठो राक्षसी आकृति ठड्याइन्छ । त्यसका तीनवटा खुट्टा हुन्छन् । शरीर विशाल छ । अनि साँझ परेपछि त्यही आकृतिलाई टोलवासीले घिसार्दै दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् र आगो लगाएर जलाउँछन् । काठमाडौँमा वर्सेनि देखिने यो दृश्य गथाँमुगः पर्वको हो । गथाँमुगः पर्व अहिले गैर नेवार समुदायबीच गठेमंगलको नामले परिचित भइरहेको छ । गथाँमुगः काठमाडौं उपत्यकाको नेवार समुदायको महत्वपूर्ण सांस्कृतिक पर्व हो ।

यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको एउटा सबैभन्दा चर्चित किंवदन्ति छ । जुन घण्टाकर्ण नाम गरेको अत्याचारी राक्षससँग सम्बन्धित रहेको छ । किंवदन्ती अनुसार घण्टाकर्ण यति ठूलो अत्याचारी थियो कि बाटो हिँड्ने मानिससँग जबर्जस्ती कर उठाउँथ्यो, दुःख दिन्थ्यो र समाजलाई आतंकित बनाएको थियो । धार्मिक मन्त्र वा पवित्र कुरा सुन्न उसलाई मनै पर्दैन थियो । त्यसैले यस्ता कुरा सुन्न नपरोस् भनेर उसले आफ्ना दुवै कानमा ठूला घण्टा झुन्ड्याएको थियो ।

जब उ हिड्थ्यो ती घण्टा ठूलो आवाज निकालेर बज्थे । त्यसैले उसको नाम नै घण्टाकर्ण रहन गएको विश्वास गरिन्छ । तर यो किंवदन्तिमा पनि ट्वीस्ट आउँछ । एकदिन अत्याचारी घण्टाकर्णको अन्त्य हुन्छ । एक दिन एक चतुर तान्त्रिकले घण्टाकर्णलाई छलपूर्वक दलदलमा फसाउने योजना बनाउँछन् । राक्षस दलदलमा नराम्ररी फस्छ । निस्कन नसकेपछि वर्षौंदेखि उसको आतंक सहिरहेका मानिसहरूले ढुंगा र माटो प्रहार गरेर उसको अन्त्य गरिदिन्छन् । यही सामूहिक विजयको सम्झना र खुशीयालीमा गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने परम्परा शुरु भएको जनविश्वास रहेको छ । त्यसैले हरेक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायमा गथाँमुगःको बेग्लै रौनक शुरु हुन्छ । काठमाडौं होस्, भक्तपुर होस् वा ललितपु, टोलटोलमा यसको छुट्टै चहलपहल देखिन्छ । घरका ढोकामा फलामको औंठी वा अन्य सुरक्षात्मक वस्तु राख्ने, घर सफा गर्ने, चोकमा राक्षसको आकृति बनाउने तथा विभिन्न परम्परागत विधि पूरा गर्ने चलन छ । कतिपय स्थानमा बालबालिका र युवाहरू घरघरमा गएर सहयोग वा दान संकलन गर्छन् ।

कतै परम्परागत गीत, बाजागाजा र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकाको वातावरणलाई थप जीवन्त र सांस्कृतिक बनाउँछ । यो पर्व मनाउने क्रममा दिनभर तयार गरिएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतीकात्मक आकृतिलाई साँझतिर टोलवासी मिलेर तानेर दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् । त्यसपछि विधिपूर्वक त्यसलाई जलाइन्छ । यसरी जलाइएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतिक पर्वको निरन्तरताको रुपमा मात्रै रहेको छैन । यसको सांकेतिक अर्थ खराब शक्तिमाथि असल शक्तिको विजयको प्रतीक पनि हो । रोगव्याधि, भूतप्रेत, अशुभ शक्ति र नकारात्मक ऊर्जा घर तथा समाजबाट टाढा जाओस् भन्ने धार्मिक विश्वास पनि यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको छ । गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने क्रममा काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका टोल बस्तीहरूमा यसको आफ्नै स्थानीय शैली र परम्परा भेटिन्छ ।

काठमाडौंका पुराना नेवारी टोलदेखि भक्तपुरका ऐतिहासिक बस्ती र ललितपुरका परम्परागत चोकसम्म गथाँमुगःले उपत्यकाको साझा सांस्कृतिक सम्पदालाई जिवित राखेको छ । आजको आधुनिक काठमाडौँमा इन्टरनेट, मोबाइल, सामाजिक सञ्जाल र व्यस्त जीवनशैलीबीच पनि अमूल्य निधिका रुपमा रहेका यस्ता जात्रा तथा पर्वहरुले निरन्तरता पाइरहेका छन् । त्यसैले हरेक जात्रा वा पर्वजस्तै गथाँमुगःको दिन साँझपख काठमाडौँका नेवारी वस्ती वा चोकमा घण्टाकर्णको आकृति आगोमा जलिरहेको देख्न पाइन्छ । यही कारण सयौँ वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आज पनि काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका गल्ली गल्लीमा उस्तै जीवन्त छ ।

articles.title: राडारमा गंगा, भानु र प्रकाश, देउवा–प्रचण्डका स्वकीयविरुद्ध अख्तियारको अनुसन्धान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अख्तियार सक्रिय बनेको छ। स–साना मुद्दामा अल्झिने गरेको अख्तियार पछिल्लो समय ठूला भनिएकाहरुसम्म पुग्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको छ। रत, अख्तियारले चालेका यस्ता कदमहरु कति सफल वा असफल त्यसको लेखाजोखा छुट्टे होला तर, शंका लागेका र आरोप खेपेकामाथिको अनुसन्धान हघि बढ्दा यसको प्रभावकारितामाथिका चासोहरु बढेका छन् ।

अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले दुईजना पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्रीहरुका स्वकीय सचिव र पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री आरजु राणा देउवाका पूर्वसहयोगीमाथि अनुसन्धान अघि बढाएको छ । अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेरबहादुर देउवाका स्वकिय सचिव भानु देउवा र पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री प्रचण्डकी छोरी समेत रहेकी स्वकिय सचिव गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

यतिमात्रै नभई अख्तियारले पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री तथा देउवा पत्नी आरजु राणा देउवाका सहयोगी समेत रहेका सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशसभाका सदस्य प्रकाश बहादुर देउवामाथि पनि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। जसमध्ये प्रकाश अहिले पनि अमेरिकामै रहेका छन्। प्रकाश आरजुको निकट सहयोगी रहेको बताइन्छ भने उनी २०७९ मा सम्पन्न प्रदेशसभा निर्वाचनमा कैलाली क्षेत्र नम्बर–५ (२) बाट प्रदेश सभामा निर्वाचित भएका थिए । उनी २०७९ माघमा प्रदेशको भौतिक पूर्वाधार विकास मन्त्री बनेका थिए । प्रकाश र भानु दुबै देउवाका भतिजहरु हुन्।

अनुसन्धान जारी

अख्तियारले तीनजनाविरुद्ध नै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र भ्रष्टाचारसम्बन्धि कसुरमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको बताइन्छ। प्रकाशविरुद्ध पूर्वमन्त्री समेत भइसकेकाले भ्रष्टाचार र सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र गंगा र भानुविरुद्ध भने सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको अनुसन्धान चलिरहेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ ।

प्रकाश देउवाविरुद्धको अनुसन्धान कसरी ?

प्रकाश देउवा अहिले अमेरिकामा छन्। उपचारका लागि भन्दै अमेरिका पुगेका प्रकाश अहिलेसम्म नेपाल फर्किएका छैनन्। उनी प्रदेश सांसद समेत भएपनि लामो समय संसदमा अनुपस्थित रहँदै आएका छन्। धेरैले उनको सेवा सुविधा नै कटौति हुनुपर्ने माग गरिरहेको बेला प्रदेश संसद सचिवालयले यसबारे थप बुझ्ने काम भइरहेकोबाहेक जवाफ दिने गरेको देखिन्न। भने तलव रोक्का गर्ने प्रावधान नै नरहेको भन्ने गरेको छ। यता, अख्तियारले पनि प्रकाश अमेरिकामा भएकोबाहेक सूचना प्राप्त गर्न सकेको देखिन्न। उनीविरुद्ध अख्तियारले अनुसन्धानका निम्ति फारम भराउने गरि तयारी गरिरहेको बताइन्छ ।

भानु देउवा र गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध के हुँदैछ ?

भानु र गंगाबारे अनुसन्धान गर्न सम्पत्ति शुद्धीकरण अनुसन्धान विभागले पत्राचार गरेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ। एकहप्ताअघि मात्रै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको पत्र प्राप्त गरेको अख्तियारको दाबी छ। योसंगै अख्तियारले विभिन्न विभागमा उनीहरुको सम्पत्ति विवरण माग गर्दै पत्राचार समेत गरिसकेको बताइएको छ। सम्पत्ति विवरण संकलनपश्चात मात्रै उनीहरुलाई सम्पत्ति सम्बन्धि फारम भराउने र बयान लिने काम थाल्ने अख्तियारको जिकिर छ । यता, अख्तियारका अधिकारीहरुले उनीहरुको बैंक विवरण र कारोबारको विवरण एकीकृत गरिरहेको समेत बताइन्छ।

केपी ओलीका स्वकियविरुद्ध पनि अनुसन्धान

अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री केपी ओलीका स्वकिय राजेश बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। गएको जेठ अन्तिम सातादेखि अनुसन्धान शुरु गरेको अख्तियारले के गरिरहेको छ भन्ने प्रगति विवरण सार्वजनिक रुपमा दिने गरेको छैन् ।

बज्राचार्यले अकुत सम्पत्ति आर्जन गरेको आरोपमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको अख्तियारले उनलाई फारम भराउनेदेखि बयान लिने काम समेत गरिसकेको बताइन्छ। बज्राचार्यले सम्पत्ति विवरण सम्बन्धी १३ पन्ने फारम भरेर अख्तियारमा बुझाइ सकेका छन् । बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध यति समूहको थामसेर्कु ट्रेकिङले दरबारमार्गस्थित नेपाल ट्रस्टको जग्गा लिजमा लैजादा अनियमितता गरेको आरोप छ। बज्राचार्यकी पत्नी रश्मि शाक्यले यति समूहबाट बालकोटस्थित रोज भिलेज हाउजिङभित्रको झण्डै चार आना जग्गामा बनेको घर घुस बापत लिएको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)को अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्ष छ । यहि विवरण देखाउदै सीआइबीले नै अख्तियारलाई लेखि पठाएपछि अनुसन्धान अघि बढिरहेको छ । उसोतः सम्पत्ति विवरणमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्दा गैरकानुनी रूपमा आर्जन गरेको भेटिएमा आयोगले भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन २०५९ अनुसार विशेष अदालतमा मुद्दा दायर गर्न सक्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था छ । अहिले आयोगले गरिरहेको अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्षपछि मात्रै अभियोजन हुने नहुने विषय टुंगो लाग्नेछ।

अख्तियारमाथि भरोसा कि प्रश्न ?

अख्तियारले गरिरहेका अनुसन्धान र अभियोजन कति प्रतिशत अदालतबाट प्रमाणित हुन्छन्? पछिल्लो समय यो प्रश्न उठिरहेको छ। अख्तियारले अभियोजनलाई कर्मकाण्डी बनाउने गरेको आरोप समेत लाग्ने गरेको छ। यस्तोमा अख्तियारले अभियोजनका लागि समय लिएपनि परिपक्क अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने र अभियोजनमा समेत विशेष ध्यान दिनुपर्ने बताइन्छ। तर, अख्तियारमाथि कार्यपालिकाको हस्तक्षेपका कारण पनि अनुसन्धान प्रभावकारी हुनेमा शंका भने देखिन्छ। तर, अख्तियारले आफ्नो शाख जोगाउने र गैरकानूनी सम्पत्ति आर्जन र भ्रष्टाचार नियन्त्रणमा उल्लेख्य भूमिका खेल्नुपर्ने संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाको पालना कसरी गर्छ भन्ने प्रश्न र भरोसा कायमै देखिन्छ।

articles.title: याडियाका तीन नयाँ स्मार्ट विद्युतीय स्कुटर नेपाली बजारमा, १० हजार छुटको अफर
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालका लागि याडिया (YADEA) को आधिकारिक वितरक कुजु नेपाल प्रा. लि. ले नयाँ पुस्ताका GS70, GT70 र GTM90 विद्युतीय स्कुटरहरू नेपाली बजारमा औपचारिक रूपमा सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। आधुनिक प्रविधि, उत्कृष्ट कार्यक्षमता र नेपाली सडक अनुकूल डिजाइन गरिएका यी स्कुटरहरूले दैनिक सहरी यात्रादेखि लामो दूरीको यात्रासम्मका फरक-फरक आवश्यकता पूरा गर्ने कम्पनीको भनाइ छ।

सार्वजनिक गरिएका तीन मोडेलमध्ये GS70 लाई दैनिक सहरी यात्राका लागि किफायती विकल्पका रूपमा तयार पारिएको छ। यसमा २.१ kWh LFP ब्याट्री र २.८ kW पिक मोटर दिइएको छ, जसले एकपटकको पूर्ण चार्जमा १०५ किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज प्रदान गर्छ। लामो दूरीको यात्रा गर्नेहरूका लागि GT70 उपयुक्त छ, जसमा ५.७ kWh को डुअल LFP ब्याट्री (३.६ kWh फिक्स्ड र २.१ kWh रिमुभेबल) तथा ३.७ kW पिक मोटर रहेको छ। यसले २२० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ भने रिमुभेबल ब्याट्रीका कारण घर वा कार्यालयमा सहजै चार्ज गर्न सकिन्छ। प्रिमियम श्रेणीको GTM90 मा ३.६ kWh लिथियम ब्याट्री र ५ kW पिक मोटर जडान गरिएको छ, जसले ८० किमि प्रतिघण्टाको उच्च गति र १५० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ।

प्रविधि र सुरक्षाका हिसाबले यी नयाँ स्कुटरहरू निकै आधुनिक छन्। ती सबैमा TFT स्मार्ट डिस्प्ले, ब्लुटुथ कनेक्टिभिटी, मोबाइल नेभिगेसन मिररिङ, याडिया स्मार्ट एप, कि-लेस प्रणाली र ५ जनासम्म प्रयोग गर्न मिल्ने 'फ्यामिली सेयरिङ' सुविधा उपलब्ध छ। यात्रालाई थप सुरक्षित र सहज बनाउन ट्र्याक्सन कन्ट्रोल सिस्टम (TCS), क्रुज कन्ट्रोल, हिल होल्ड, हिल डिसेन्ट कन्ट्रोल र डुअल डिस्क ब्रेकजस्ता अत्याधुनिक प्रविधि समावेश गरिएका छन्।

कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलका ब्याट्रीमा ३ वर्ष वा ५०,००० किलोमिटरसम्मको दीर्घकालीन वारेन्टी प्रदान गरेको छ। हाल यी स्कुटरहरू देशभर रहेका २० वटा आधिकारिक याडिया डिलरशिपहरू मार्फत उपलब्ध छन्। साथै, सार्वजनिक गरिएको अवसरमा नाइमा अटो शो (NAIMA Auto Show) सम्म लागू हुने गरी कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलमा रु. १०,००० को विशेष नगद छुट दिएको छ। ग्राहकहरूले नजिकैको शोरुममा गई टेस्ट राइड तथा फाइनान्सिङ सुविधाबारे थप जानकारी लिन सक्नेछन्।

articles.title: खल्तीबाट डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा दैनिक १ लाख र बम्परमा १० लाख जित्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । आईएमई खल्ती लिमिटेडले अर्थ मन्त्रालयअन्तर्गतको आन्तरिक राजस्व विभागद्वारा सञ्चालित ‘करदाता प्रोत्साहन उपहार कार्यक्रम, २०८३’ मा आफ्ना प्रयोगकर्तालाई सहभागी गराउने भएको छ। खल्तीमार्फत रु १०० भन्दा बढीको योग्य डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा ग्राहकहरू स्वतः दैनिक तथा पाक्षिक उपहार छनोटमा सहभागी हुनेछन्।

यस कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत दैनिक एक जना विजेताले कर कट्टीपछि रु. १ लाख र प्रत्येक १५ दिनमा एक जना बम्पर विजेताले रु १० लाख प्राप्त गर्नेछन्। भुक्तानीको विवरण सुरक्षित रूपमा राजस्व विभागको प्रणालीमा पुग्ने र उपहार कुपन स्वतः सिर्जना भई खल्ती एपमै देखिने व्यवस्था मिलाइएको छ। विभागले प्रत्येक महिनाको १ र १६ गते स्वचालित प्रणालीबाट विजेता छनोट गरी एसएमएस, इमेल तथा खल्तीमार्फत जानकारी गराउनेछ।

बिलमा आधारित कारोबार प्रवर्द्धन गरी डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्र र राष्ट्रिय राजस्व प्रणालीलाई सुदृढ बनाउने लक्ष्यका साथ यो सहकार्य गरिएको आईएमई खल्तीका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रवीण रेग्मीले बताएका छन्।

articles.title: Finance Ministry delays forwarding MCA Nepal’s request to extend MCC projects
articles.summary:
The Ministry of Finance has held up a request from the Millennium Challenge Account Nepal (MCA-Nepal) for a one-year extension of US-funded infrastructure projects, with the proposal yet to reach the US government’s Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC).

MCA-Nepal sent the request to the ministry mid-May, asking it to formally approach MCC headquarters for an extension of the $747 million projects, which include a 315-km transmission line and road upgrade works.

A senior finance ministry official told the Post that they had received a letter on behalf of MCA-Nepal but had not yet been forwarded to MCC headquarters. “It is still under discussion,” the official told the Post, without disclosing why the request had been held up or when it would be sent.

The MCA-Nepal board member said MCA-Nepal sent the request to the Finance Ministry, which serves as the liaison ministry and must formally approach the MCC headquarters on Nepal’s behalf. The finance secretary heads the MCA-Nepal board.

Under the MCC Compact, the projects are supposed to be completed by August 30, 2028. But MCA-Nepal says implementation has been delayed by about 14 months because of the US government’s temporary suspension of MCC operations and the cancellation and re-tendering of contracts for the transmission line.

“Due to some reasons, we have already sought a one-year term extension for the completion of the two projects,” said a senior MCA-Nepal board member who is not authorised to speak to the media.

“It has been three months since MCA-Nepal sent such a request to the finance ministry, but there is no information about the term extension,” the board member said.

Once the finance ministry forwards the request, the MCC headquarters will review the reasons cited by MCA-Nepal and decide whether to grant the extension.

In its letter, MCA-Nepal stated that due to some unavoidable circumstances, including US President Donald Trump’s decision in July 2025 to pause US foreign assistance and halt MCC payments. The suspension put the projects in limbo for several months before the administration decided in July 2025 to allow MCC’s global operations, including in Nepal, to continue.

MCA-Nepal also cited the cancellation of bids in October 2023 for construction of the 315-km 400kV transmission line after all bidders quoted prices substantially above the estimated cost.

Following the cancellation, MCA-Nepal had to restart the bidding process. It took almost nine months to award a fresh contract, an MCA-Nepal official told the Post.

The official said MCC headquarters is positive about the term extension and that a new US law could also facilitate the extension.

“First, the MCC headquarters itself is positive because our reasons are grounded and valid. Second, the Trump administration has introduced a new law that permits a one-year term extension to the projects currently in operation in four countries,” the official said.

MCA-Nepal is a government agency set up to manage the MCC Compact in Nepal.

The five-year compact was signed between the government of Nepal and MCC in September 2017. The US initially committed $500 million in grants, while Nepal agreed to contribute $150 million, which was later jacked up to $197 million. The total investment in two projects has therefore reached $697 million. The MCC board had also agreed to provide an additional $50 million to cover a funding gap, potentially taking the total value of the compact to $747 million.

Dragged into controversy, the compact was ratified by the House of Representatives in February 2022 and entered into force on August 30, 2023.

MCA-Nepal is seeking more time mainly because of delays in getting the projects off the ground. But officials say implementation continues to face problems, especially in the transmission line project.

The road project is progressing smoothly, they said. But the transmission line project has been held up by problems with land acquisition, compensation, construction quality and compliance with environmental rules.

Construction of substations has also raised quality concerns. Many people have yet to receive compensation for their land acquired for the transmission line’s right of way, according to officials. “So far compensation has been distributed for only 18 km of the transmission line’s right of way,” an official told the Post, adding, “How can contractors start work until they get the site clearance?”

“Land acquisition is still facing hurdles and has not been resolved despite a large team and resources being mobilised on the ground,” an official who regularly monitors the MCC projects from both the centre and the field.

“The way compensation is being provided to affected families and land owners under the MCC project could create problems for future transmission line projects. We may not be able to afford similar levels of compensation in other projects,” the official said.

articles.title: Durgalal Shrestha, poet who championed Nepal Bhasha literature, dies at 93
articles.summary:
Poet and lyricist Durgalal Shrestha, one of the best-known poets of modern Nepal Bhasha literature, died at his home in Budhanilkantha on Sunday night. He was 93.

Kishan Sundar Malla, chancellor of the Nepal Bhasha Academy and a close associate of Shrestha, said the poet’s death was a major loss to Nepal Bhasha literature. “He was born to write,” said Malla, describing Shrestha as a son of Saraswati, the Hindu goddess of learning.

Born in Nhyakatol in central Kathmandu in Nepal Sambat 1057, Shrestha was the son of Aashamoti and Ganesh Lal. He entered the literary world by writing plays, and in Nepal Sambat 1075, his poem ‘Santwana’ was published in Dharmodaya magazine. He later became best known as a poet, although he was also a lyricist, playwright and translator. In 2003, the Nepal Bhasha Parishad conferred Shrestha with the title of Janakavi—people’s poet.

Shrestha often recalled with pride that he wrote, directed and acted in a play in Nepal Bhasha when he was only 11. Street theatre was common in Kathmandu neighbourhoods at the time, and the experience began his long literary career.

Although he wrote poems, songs, plays, essays and translations, Shrestha became best known as a poet. His writing earned him the title Janakabi, or people’s poet, because his language was accessible to ordinary readers while carrying strong emotions and ideas.

Essayist Ramesh Kaji Sthapit, who followed Shrestha’s literary career closely, said the most striking quality of his poetry was its musicality. “His poems were like songs,” said Sthapit. Almost all could be sung because they had rhythm and melody.

Shrestha’s first book, ‘Chiniyamha Kisicha’, was a collection of children’s poems and became one of the best-selling books published in Nepal Bhasha. He went on to publish more than a dozen collections of poems and songs. His writing often dealt with nationalism, language and community advancement.

The veteran poet and lyricist also wrote in Nepali. His song ‘Phoolko Aankhama Phoolai Sansar’ remains among his best-known works.

Sthapit said Shrestha’s work as a playwright was often overshadowed by his poetry and songs. “His pen perhaps ran even faster for plays than for poems,” he said. “His plays were equally strong, but his identity as a poet and lyricist covered them.”

For Shrestha, literature was also a form of cultural activism. After Radio Nepal stopped broadcasting news in Nepal Bhasha in 1965, he became an active participant in the movement against the state’s one-language policy. Literary conferences were organised across Kathmandu Valley neighbourhoods for about a year against the policy, and Shrestha actively took part in them. His poems and songs from that period became part of the wider campaign for recognition of Nepal Bhasha.

Shrestha remained active in organisations devoted to Nepal Bhasha and Newari cultural rights, and became a founding member of Nepal Bhasa Manka Khala.

Shrestha’s influence extended beyond books. His neat handwriting became so closely associated with him that a type font was later named after him. His poems and songs have travelled beyond Nepal through translations.

Shresha’s funeral is scheduled for Tuesday; colleagues, admirers and members of the Nepal Bhasha community are expected to gather to pay their final respects. His body will be kept at the Nepal Bhasha Manka Khala building in Bijeshwari before a funeral procession and cremation at Karnadeep.

For a literary community that saw him as both a creator and an advocate, Shrestha’s death marks the end of an unusually long career—one that began with a child’s neighbourhood play and grew into a lifelong effort to make language, literature and identity speak to ordinary people.

articles.title: PMO scrutiny of Nepal Telecom billing tender raises concerns over interference
articles.summary:
The prime minister’s office (PMO) has begun examining the tender process and technical specifications for Nepal Telecom’s proposed new billing system, prompting concerns within the state-owned operator over what employees describe as growing external involvement in technical and procurement decisions.

The information technology section of the PMO instructed the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology on May 27 to provide documents related to the procurement, with a copy sent to Nepal Telecom. The requested records include procurement documents, system design and architecture diagrams, geographic information system frameworks and details of the company’s 4G/LTE operations.

The review is being conducted by an information technology study task force under the PMO, according to Hemraj Aryal, PMO spokesman.

“Our IT study task force is reviewing the issues related with the billing system,” Aryal told Kantipur. “However, a comprehensive report detailing specific findings has not yet been submitted. Detailed insights will be accessible once the task force concludes its evaluation.”

Aryal said the review was a routine assessment and was not intended to interfere with Nepal Telecom’s procurement or operations.

“It is merely a standard study intended to assess the overall status of public information technology infrastructure,” he said. “The task force was previously constituted to review various IT systems across state organs. This routine assessment is unlikely to halt or impede Nepal Telecom’s ongoing operational procedures.”

The explanation has done little to ease concerns among senior Nepal Telecom officials, who argue that decisions involving the company’s core systems should be guided by established technical and procurement processes rather than political or administrative intervention.

The scrutiny comes as Nepal Telecom prepares fresh tender documents for a new billing system estimated to cost around Rs5 billion. Previous attempts to procure the system were stalled by legal challenges, complaints over tender specifications and administrative decisions.

The company’s board has recently delegated full authority to the managing director to execute the procurement, apparently to streamline decision-making and prevent further delays.

Nepal Telecom joint spokesperson Prakschet Thapa Chhetri said preparations for the revised tender were under way.

“Our technical team is working intensively. Given the intricate and highly sensitive nature of this procurement, thorough preparation is mandatory,” he said. “Once finalised, the details will be released transparently into the public domain. We view the prime minister’s office’s interest as a constructive and supportive gesture.”

Dispute over splitting the system

The latest scrutiny followed a request from the IT study task force for historical and current records relating to Nepal Telecom’s billing and other systems. The company initially submitted digital copies of tender documents by email, but officials at Singha Durbar later asked telecom representatives to provide physical copies.

“The tender documents were already available publicly on the Public Procurement Monitoring Office website,” said an employee familiar with the process, speaking on condition of anonymity. “Yet, after being pressured by central officials, our staff spent hours photocopying thousands of pages of technical archives.”

The request has also revived an earlier debate over whether Nepal Telecom should procure the billing system as a single integrated platform or split it into separate contracts. According to telecom officials, the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, reflecting views from the prime minister’s office, initially favoured separating the system’s software and hardware, with part of the software to be potentially developed by domestic companies.

Under the proposed model, Nepal Telecom would retain the Online Charging System (OCS) and hardware infrastructure, while the Business Support System (BSS) would be procured or developed separately.

The proposal met resistance from Nepal Telecom’s management and employee unions, who argued that the billing platform is not simply a commercial software application but a core telecommunications system closely linked to customer identities, SIM registration, international roaming and real-time usage information. Separating the integrated system, they said, could create gaps in responsibility during failures and increase security and operational risks.

“This infrastructure integrates international roaming protocols, real-time location tracking, and critical socio-economic indicators,” said Lokendra Paneru, general secretary of the Nepal Telecom Workers’ Union. “It handles live profiles and data streams involving everyone, from high-ranking government officials to ordinary citizens. Approaching it casually poses immense national risks.”

Telecom engineers have similarly argued that the OCS and BSS, while performing different functions, operate within an integrated architecture and require coordinated hardware, software and technical support.

Following technical briefings from Nepal Telecom, officials at the prime minister’s office have reportedly softened their earlier position.

A senior PMO official, speaking on condition of anonymity, acknowledged that separate procurement had previously been proposed.

“A joint proposal had previously been drafted by ministry leadership and prime minister’s advisers recommending the split procurement model,” the official said. “However, Nepal Telecom’s technical team maintained a firm stance that breaking up an integrated architecture creates severe accountability gaps during system failures.”

The dispute has thus moved beyond whether the government should scrutinise a major public procurement. It has raised a broader question over how far administrative oversight should extend into technical decisions at a state-owned telecommunications operator, particularly as delays could jeopardise the replacement of an ageing system.

Previous tenders faced legal hurdles

The current procurement is the latest attempt to replace Nepal Telecom’s ageing billing infrastructure, which was installed in 2011 by Chinese technology company AsiaInfo-Linkage Technologies. The system has remained in operation through successive contract extensions, with the current arrangement due to expire in 2027.

Efforts to replace it have been dogged by controversy and legal challenges. Earlier tender specifications were criticised for allegedly favouring Huawei Technologies, which already supplies significant network infrastructure to Nepal Telecom. Critics argued that awarding both network infrastructure and billing functions to the same vendor could deepen vendor lock-in and create risks involving competition, system dependence and data security.

The dispute eventually reached the Supreme Court, which directed Nepal Telecom to reduce its dependence on a single vendor and ensure adequate safeguards for privacy and data security.

Despite the ruling, subsequent technical evaluations again qualified Huawei while disqualifying other bidders, including Whale Cloud, renewing questions over whether the tender requirements allowed sufficient competition.

A Huawei Nepal representative defended the limited participation of international vendors, saying major global suppliers such as Ericsson, Oracle and CSG rarely participate in Nepal government tenders. That, the representative said, leaves a limited pool of vendors capable of meeting Nepal Telecom’s technical requirements.

The procurement also came under scrutiny from within the government. In November 2025, the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology formed an investigation panel led by former secretary Mani Ram Gelal after complaints alleging manipulation of the tender process.

The panel’s report warned that rigid qualification criteria could favour particular bidders and raised concerns over outdated procurement arrangements and potential financial liabilities for the state-owned company. The findings added to questions over how Nepal Telecom should structure a procurement involving a system that is both technically complex and critical to its daily operations.

The billing division had previously faced scrutiny from the Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority. In May 2024, the anti-graft body filed corruption charges against former Nepal Telecom managing director Sunil Poudel and former chief business officer Sangeeta Pahadi Aryal over alleged irregularities in maintenance contracts. Pahadi Aryal was later cleared of the charges by the court and has since returned to an executive leadership role at Nepal Telecom.

Delays threaten transition

The prolonged procurement process has increased pressure on Nepal Telecom to replace its ageing system before the current contract expires.

Replacing a billing platform of this scale involves migrating large volumes of customer and network data, testing and integrating the new system, and running the old and new platforms in parallel. Nepal Telecom officials say a complex migration and data transfer requires at least 24 months of operational preparation.

Any further delay in awarding the contract could therefore leave less time for a controlled transition before the existing arrangement expires in 2027.

The concern is not only financial. A billing system processes subscriber information, usage records, account balances, charging and other functions essential to a telecommunications operator. Problems during migration could affect customers nationwide, disrupt revenue collection and compromise service management.

Nepal Telecom’s legacy infrastructure has already experienced periodic problems, with disruptions affecting mobile and data services. The Nepal Telecommunications Authority (NTA) has intervened following complaints and directed the operator to strengthen backup arrangements.

“The authority dispatched technical inspection teams to monitor network failures firsthand and directed Nepal Telecom to maintain backup systems,” said NTA spokesperson Min Prasad Aryal. “Our primary focus remains enforcing statutory quality-of-service mandates and compliance with license obligations.”

Nepal Telecom says the existing system has not caused an immediate financial loss, but continued reliance on ageing infrastructure could constrain its ability to expand services and handle growing traffic.

Joint spokesperson Thapa said previous attempts to launch a replacement tender had been stalled by administrative and legal challenges.

“We attempted to launch new tenders in the past, but administrative and legal challenges stalled progress, forcing us to make temporary fixes to the existing hardware,” he said. “If we fail to upgrade the core infrastructure systematically, network performance will deteriorate, directly impacting customer service efficiency across the country.”

The need for a replacement is also linked to Nepal Telecom’s plans to expand next-generation services, including 5G. A modern billing platform would be expected to handle more complex products, real-time charging and higher transaction volumes as data use grows.

For Nepal Telecom, the challenge is therefore to replace a system approaching the end of its extended contractual life without introducing new technological dependencies or operational vulnerabilities.

The prime minister’s office maintains that its involvement is limited to a technical review, while Nepal Telecom says it welcomes scrutiny and intends to conduct the procurement transparently.

articles.title: Nepali orthodox tea is in demand, but its workforce is shrinking
articles.summary:
The tea bushes at the Pathibhara Tea Estate, spread across 51 hectares in Panchthar, an eastern hill district, are flush with fresh shoots these days.

The estate plucks and processes the ‘two leaves and a bud’ used to make high-quality premium loose-leaf tea, which it exports to third-country markets.

The factory has the capacity to employ up to 50 workers a day. However, only 10 to 15 workers are currently working at the estate in Falelung and Yangwarak rural municipalities.

Pathibhara, located at Charibhanjyang, is not alone. Most tea gardens in eastern Nepal are currently waiting for workers to pluck tea leaves. Tea gardens and factories pay workers Rs110 per kg for plucking leaves. In addition, workers receive extra wages for withering, rolling, processing, sorting and packaging tea in the mornings and evenings.

“Despite these incentives, tea gardens are facing a shortage of workers,” said Rajan Bhattarai, proprietor of the tea estate.

Experienced workers employed in the tea sector can normally earn up to Rs40,000 a month, including accommodation.

For Shashikala Rai from ward 2 of Falelung Rural Municipality who was plucking tea leaves, working on the hillside is not as strenuous as going abroad and working in the heat.

“At a time when our brothers and sisters are wandering around villages saying there are no job opportunities, and are forced to do strenuous work in 40-degree [Celsius] heat abroad, we are working in the cool and scenic tea gardens here,” she said.

“The earning is not bad either. We earn up to Rs40,000 a month. With such opportunities available, why go abroad?” said Rai. According to her, women workers account for a large share of those involved in tea plucking and processing.

In recent years, an increasing number of both men and women have been going abroad for employment. Most women who remain in the villages are increasingly moving to district headquarters and urban areas to live with their children for their education.

This has created a shortage of workers in small and medium-sized factories and tea gardens operating in rural areas.

Annually, nearly 800,000 Nepalis go abroad in search of jobs, leaving Nepal’s farm sector without sufficient manpower. In recent years, tea estates in eastern Nepal have been hit hard by the shortage of workers.

There are around 60,000 tea workers across eastern districts such as Ilam, Panchthar and Jhapa. Most are temporary or daily-wage labourers, meaning they miss out on steady year-round income and robust benefits. As a result, tea work has not been attractive to many.

Jeet Bahadur Limbu, another tea worker, said tea gardens offer employment for nine months of the year, except for the three-month period from early November to January. Limbu, however, said he is comfortable with the earnings.

“It is frustrating to see young people leaving the country saying they are unemployed despite such opportunities being available here,” Limbu said.

Organic orthodox tea produced here without using chemical fertilisers and pesticides is reaching international markets. Although production and market prospects are expanding, a shortage of workers is constraining the capacity of tea gardens.

Tea gardens producing orthodox tea that sell for Rs5,000 to Rs7,000 per kilogram in overseas markets are currently waiting for workers.

The tea leaves produced at Pathibhara and other tea gardens in Panchthar are processed into high-quality organic orthodox tea.

Bhattarai said tea produced without chemical fertilisers and pesticides comes in more than 10 flavours, with natural sweetness, a high-altitude aroma and a distinctive taste, generating demand in third-country markets. He said the tea is exported to international markets including the United States, Germany, France, Japan, South Korea and China.

According to data from the Tea Expansion Project (Chiya Bistar Yojana) in Lalikharka, Panchthar, a government-established tea garden managed by the National Tea and Coffee Development Board, Panchthar has six tea estates and factories and 10 small tea producer groups.

Tea is cultivated on 600 hectares across the district by estates and individual farmers. Although around 2,000 farmers are involved in tea farming through factories and producer groups, factories and tea gardens are facing a shortage of workers.

According to operators, Pathibhara alone produces around 8,000 kg of tea annually.

Bhattarai said the estate has developed the capacity to produce more than 12,000 kg if there is no shortage of workers, but the labour shortage is likely to affect production.

Demand for Nepali organic tea is increasing in international markets. Despite good local income, residential accommodation, and regular employment opportunities, the shortage of workers is delaying the plucking of tea shoots, Bhattarai said.

Nepal exports more than 88 percent of its orthodox tea to India, leaving only a small fraction for third-country markets.

Nepal processes 7,838 tonnes of orthodox tea annually. Exports of orthodox tea to third countries account for 11.4 percent. Orthodox tea uses traditional methods, including plucking, withering, rolling, oxidation and drying.

There are two types of exports: organic certified and uncertified. The export of organic-certified orthodox tea to third countries accounts for 21.63 percent.

A report by Nepal Rastra Bank highlights that Nepali organic orthodox tea has significant potential in Japan, China, the Netherlands, Canada, Russia, Poland, Turkey and South Korea.

Despite its potential, Nepali organic tea faces multiple challenges, including difficulties in marketisation, fair pricing, access to credit facilities and a lack of skilled workers.

Other obstacles include a lack of technical assistance, insurance and incentives for organic production. These challenges hinder orthodox tea entrepreneurs from unlocking potential new markets.

According to the central bank report, seven factories export to Japan, four to China, two to the United States and eight to other countries. The study included 84 orthodox tea factories and 42 orthodox tea growers.

In September 2020, Nepal’s orthodox tea received its own trademark, 157 years after the country began growing it. The trademark includes the words “Nepal Tea Quality from the Himalayas.” Koshi province has 100 orthodox tea processing factories, 21 of which are organically certified.

articles.title: Speaker instructs PM Shah to attend parliament, answer lawmakers
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who has been absent from the House of Representatives for a long time, will now have to stand at the parliamentary rostrum and answer lawmakers’ questions. Speaker DP Aryal issued the ruling after Shah repeatedly skipped the monthly question-and-answer session required under parliamentary rules.

Speaker Aryal had to issue the ruling as Prime Minister Shah has been violating the House of Representatives regulations, which require the prime minister to answer lawmakers’ questions during the first week of every month. Lawmakers had been demanding that Shah come to parliament and clarify his position since he made controversial remarks about the border in the House of Representatives on May 31. Earlier, lawmakers had also demanded that the prime minister respond to questions during discussions on the government’s policies and programmes, but Shah had ignored their demands.

“Members of parliament have been raising this issue for a long time, and it has come to my attention,” said Speaker Aryal before directing the prime minister to attend the House and answer questions as per House of Representatives Regulations, 2026.

Speaker Aryal clarified that each parliamentary party will be guaranteed at least one question during the direct question-and-answer session. Up to 15 additional questions will be selected according to the parties’ numerical strength in the House. Lawmakers can submit written questions to the parliamentary secretariat by 1 pm on Friday.

The dispute dates back to Shah’s first appearance in the House of Representatives on May 31, when he answered questions after weeks of pressure from opposition parties. Responding to a question about Nepal-India border disputes, Shah said Nepal had also encroached on Indian territory in several places, a statement that immediately drew criticism.

“You may find this surprising, but I too only recently learned, after becoming prime minister, that Nepal has encroached on Indian territory in many places, not just India on Nepali territory,” PM Shah had said while addressing parliament.

In response to Shah’s controversial remarks, the opposition parties demanded that Shah retract the statement, provide evidence and clarify his position in parliament. They also protested against the Speaker’s handling of the session, arguing that Shah’s appearance had not followed the normal format of the monthly direct question session.

The controversy has since led to repeated deadlocks in the House. The opposition parties had already been demanding Shah’s presence after he repeatedly skipped parliamentary discussions on the government’s policies and programmes. The dispute intensified when the prime minister designated Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle to respond to lawmakers on his behalf.

The latest ruling is therefore significant for both the government and the Speaker. Aryal himself has faced criticism from opposition lawmakers, who have questioned whether he has acted independently of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party RSP), from which he came to the Speaker’s post. Critics said the opposition’s trust in Aryal had weakened over his handling of the dispute.

RSP Chairman Rabi Lamichhane, General Secretary Bipin Acharya, deputy parliamentary leader Ganesh Parajuli and chief whip Kabindra Burlakoti, among other senior leaders were present at Monday’s meeting of the House of Representatives.

CPN-UML parliamentary party deputy leader Padma Kumari Aryal welcomed Monday’s ruling. “The opposition has been seeking an answer on the same issue in parliament for a long time. I want to thank the Speaker again for issuing a ruling that ensures an answer,” she said in the House.

The ruling party also welcomed the development. RSP chief whip Burlakoti said the Speaker had coordinated with the prime minister and set a date for his appearance.

“The Speaker took the initiative and coordinated on this matter, and it has now been decided that the prime minister will come [to parliament] on August 26,” said Burlakoti. “There had been discussions and coordination, and after today’s ruling the prime minister will come to parliament and move the matter forward.”

He said the ruling could help end the dispute that had paralysed House proceedings. “The initiative to resolve the problem is positive,” he said, adding that Shah’s busy schedule should not prevent him from attending parliament.

A member of Shah’s secretariat said the prime minister had already been preparing to answer lawmakers. “The prime minister had been preparing to answer lawmakers’ questions this time. The process of collecting written questions and preparing responses was under way,” the official said. “After the Speaker issued the ruling, the prime minister will attend the House.”

Nepali Congress whip Nishcal Rai said Prime Minister Shah must use the opportunity to answer lawmakers’ questions and address the controversy over his earlier remarks. He credited the Speaker with helping hold executive accountability to parliament.

“We wanted the Speaker to issue such a ruling,” Rai said. “The Speaker has a primary responsibility to uphold parliament’s dignity and plays a key role in holding the executive accountable to the legislature.” Rai said opposition lawmakers had ended their protest because they had faith in the office of the Speaker. “We believe the prime minister will attend parliament as instructed by the Speaker, clarify his earlier remarks and, we hope, correct or withdraw them from the record,” he said.

The government’s willingness to have Shah attend parliament could ease a dispute that has dominated House proceedings since his first appearance. But Monday’s ruling also highlights how difficult it has been to enforce parliamentary procedures that require the prime minister to answer lawmakers’ questions regularly.

Before issuing the ruling, Aryal had twice visited the prime minister’s office to meet Shah and urge him to appear in parliament. According to people familiar with those meetings, the Speaker told the prime minister that it would be better for him to appear in person and answer lawmakers’ questions. Shah did not set a date, responding only that he would attend at an appropriate time.

Former parliament secretary-general Manohar Prasad Bhattarai said Speaker Aryal would not have had to issue a ruling if Prime Minister Shah had understood his responsibilities and attended parliament regularly.

“An accountable government must answer questions raised by elected representatives in parliament. This should not have needed to be said,” said Bhattarai.

Bhattarai said it would be good parliamentary practice for Shah to address national and international issues in the House. “The prime minister cannot ignore parliament. He must be accountable to the House under the Constitution, parliamentary rules, practices, and conventions,” he said.

articles.title: Nepal’s revived Industrial Security Force must ensure business protection
articles.summary:
The private sector has long served as the primary engine of the Nepali economy, generating approximately 86 percent of jobs and contributing roughly 81.55 percent to the national output. Yet, for decades, commercial enterprises have borne the brunt of broader political instability and social grievances, routinely finding themselves the first targets of arson, extortion and looting. Against this backdrop, the Government of Nepal’s recent decision to revive the Industrial Security Force (ISF) under the newly launched Private Investment Protection and Promotion Strategy is a welcome move.

Albeit late, the strategy represents the Balen Shah administration’s pragmatic shift towards acknowledging that capital accumulation cannot flourish if the physical security of enterprises is compromised. After recurring instances of civil unrest—most notably the Gen Z movement of September, which inflicted losses exceeding Rs84 billion to private businesses across the country, and the more recent arson of enterprises in Golbazar, Siraha, towards the end of July—the government seems to be attempting to rebuild the shattered confidence of the business community. This is also in line with PM Shah’s meeting with leaders of the business community on July 8.

The historical precedent of the ISF is deeply discouraging. The Armed Police Force personnel initially deployed under the ISF concept in 2012 were permanently redeployed to border regions during the Covid-19 pandemic and never returned to their industrial posts. This security vacuum, even after the pandemic ended, left major industrial corridors completely vulnerable, inducing a climate of persistent risk that stagnated private investment growth at a dismal 0.2 percent in the last fiscal year.

While declaring industrial zones as ‘peace zones’ and establishing rapid-response teams are commendable policy steps, such strategic formulation alone will not assuage the deep-seated investor scepticism. Timely amendments to laws such as the Industrial Enterprises Act, the Foreign Investment and Technology Transfer Act, and the Special Economic Zone Act also help the cause by demonstrating commendable legislative intent. However, the introduction of security strategies remains mere symbolism until the government demonstrates a resolute zero-tolerance stance against offenders through actual prosecution and punishment. The Shah administration’s ambitious economic targets—expanding the national economy to nearly $100 billion, raising per capita income to $3,000, and maintaining an average annual growth rate of 7 percent—will remain entirely unachievable if the state fails to guarantee basic property rights and physical safety.

To convert the strategic initiative of ISF into a tangible economic catalyst, the Shah government must focus on decisive, multi-layered execution. First, the deployment of the revived security force must be institutionalised through dedicated, permanent units, ensuring that personnel are never again diverted to auxiliary state duties during crises. Second, the state must establish a clear legal precedent of accountability. Legal proceedings against individuals involved in commercial vandalism must be swift, resolute and transparent, ending the decades-long culture of impunity that has surrounded targeted attacks on private enterprises.

Furthermore, the government should swiftly operationalise the proposed joint coordination and facilitation committee comprising state officials and private-sector representatives. It is incumbent that this framework empowers business leaders to directly highlight emerging security vulnerabilities before localised protests escalate into destructive violence. Combining these security measures with proactive administrative relief—such as streamlining relocation permits through Initial Environmental Examinations for damaged businesses and granting targeted tax, fee, or penalty waivers for struggling firms—will provide immediate support to the commercial landscape. Ultimately, policy declarations must translate into tangible protection on the ground. Only by guaranteeing a safe, predictable and resilient operational environment can Nepal inspire domestic enterprise, attract foreign direct investment, and place its national economy on a sustainable trajectory toward long-term prosperity.

articles.title: Building a tax system for trust, investment and prosperity
articles.summary:
The 2026-27 fiscal budget deserves appreciation for one important reason. Amid competing fiscal pressures and slowing economic activity, it has committed to launching a second generation of tax reforms. The timing could not be more appropriate. Nepal’s tax system has reached a stage where incremental changes are no longer sufficient. What is now required is a comprehensive reform agenda that restores public trust, promotes investment, broadens the tax base, and prepares the country for a rapidly changing economy.

But despite all the promise and hype around tax reforms with the change in government, there are signals of policy flip-flops, unpredictability, loss of trust, and even backsliding of earlier reforms. This is especially true with the probability of introducing multiple Value Added Tax (VAT) rates (for example, a different rate of 5 percent on electricity) and losing the fairness and equity—both horizontal and vertical—elements in the new tax tariffs or administrative measures. Moreover, the government has introduced several new tax concessions and exemptions (as summarised in sections 68 and 73 of the Budget Speech 2083–84) despite the promise of comprehensive application of the tax regime to broaden the tax base.

Nepal is not starting from scratch. The country has already witnessed the first generation of tax reforms in the 1990s. The reforms introduced in that period had three landmark departures from the earlier tax regime. First, self-assessment in income taxation shifted the relationship between taxpayers and the tax administration from official determination to voluntary compliance. Second, the introduction of a single-rate VAT, an input tax credit mechanism, and a built-in self-policing system created one of the most efficient indirect tax structures. Third, self-declaration in customs and excise moved tax administration away from excessive official discretion towards greater trust in taxpayers.

These reforms were guided by a simple philosophy: lower tax rates, a broader tax base, and greater tax equity. Moderate, universally applied tax rates were expected to encourage compliance, reduce tax evasion, and generate higher revenues without discouraging investment and economic growth. For many years, this framework served Nepal well.

The challenge today is not that the original reforms were flawed, but that their underlying principles have gradually been diluted. Over the years, substantive tax laws have increasingly been amended through annual finance acts. Frequent policy changes have depleted trust in the tax system by introducing uncertainty and unpredictability, and have made long-term business and investment decisions difficult. Equally concerning has been the proliferation of tax exemptions and concessions. Every exemption narrows the tax base, creates opportunities for leakage, and often rewards influence rather than genuine economic merit.

At the same time, tax procedures have failed to modernise to meet the needs of a digital economy. Compliance remains costly and cumbersome. Excessive paperwork, multiple reporting requirements, and outdated administrative practices increase the cost of doing business. These weaknesses have adversely affected investment, productivity, growth and employment.

Tax Reform 2.0 must, therefore, begin by restoring trust. No tax system can function efficiently unless taxpayers have confidence that tax laws are predictable, fairly administered and consistently applied. Predictability, policy stability, impartial administration and transparency should become the cornerstones of Nepal’s tax system.

Tax administration itself requires fundamental modernisation. Paperless and contactless procedures should become the norm. Full self-assessment, supported by risk-based audits and digital verification, can significantly reduce compliance costs while improving administrative efficiency. Honest taxpayers should find compliance easier, while deliberate non-compliance should become increasingly difficult through intelligent data analysis rather than excessive physical enforcement.

A comprehensive review of tax exemptions is equally essential. Most concessions should either be eliminated or subjected to transparent public disclosure through annual tax expenditure statements. Tax equity must guide reform once again. Horizontal equity requires taxpayers with similar economic capacity to bear similar tax burdens. Vertical equity demands protection of lower-income households from excessive tax incidence. Where environmental taxes such as carbon taxes are introduced, targeted budgetary compensation should protect poorer households from their regressive effects.

Digital economic activities should be brought under a tax framework by subjecting such transactions to both direct and indirect taxes based upon emerging international practices. Likewise, informal businesses should gradually be integrated into the formal tax system initially at low tax rates and with simplified procedures to formalise the economy and expand the tax base.

Technology should become the backbone of modern tax administration. Integrated databases capable of communicating with banking systems, business registries and other government databases can verify transactions intelligently while reducing unnecessary compliance costs. Artificial intelligence and advanced analytics can improve audit selection, detect fraud and strengthen revenue administration. Such modernisation requires sustained investment in reliable hardware, secure software and skilled human resources.

Tax reform must also reflect Nepal’s federal governance structure. Tax procedures should be harmonised across federal, provincial and local governments to provide an integrated nationwide tax framework to the taxpayers. Double taxation of the same transaction should be eliminated while ensuring fair revenue sharing among all three levels of government. The indirect tax structure also deserves careful review. Preserving a single VAT rate maintains simplicity and minimises disputes, while a modest reduction in the rate, combined with a broader tax base and improved compliance, could stimulate economic activity without compromising revenue.

Revenue reform should extend beyond taxation alone. Better management of non-tax revenues—including market-based pricing of natural resources, fair returns from public assets, improved utilisation of public infrastructure, and modern cash management through short-term treasury instruments—can significantly strengthen public finances.

Ultimately, tax reform is about rebuilding the social contract between the state and its citizens. People are more willing to pay taxes when they see that public resources are managed efficiently, transparently and for the common good.

A second generation of tax reform will undoubtedly demand strong commitment at both the political and organisational levels. There are no gains without pains. Every meaningful reform temporarily disrupts established interests as it realigns resources, priorities and economic and social structures. It therefore requires careful management of the political economy of reform and sustained leadership to overcome inevitable resistance.

Yet, the long-term rewards far outweigh the short-term costs. A good tax system is not one that simply collects more revenue; it is one that releases the productive resources of businesses for greater investment, innovation and employment while ensuring fairness for all. In an ideal economy, investment decisions should be driven by the economic merits of the investment itself—not by tax distortions or preferential treatments. That should be the true objective of Tax Reform 2.0.

articles.title: Journalism in the age of algorithms
articles.summary:
Who decides what becomes news today? Principally, journalists and editors play the central role in deciding which events and issues deserve public attention. But the process is changing now. The news we see, read and engage with is being increasingly shaped by forces beyond the newsroom. This shift raises a question: Who, or what, is now influencing the news production process and overall news agenda?

Algorithms at present influence every stage of news production, distribution and consumption. For example, many newsrooms globally use AI and algorithms to identify potential news stories even before journalists start collecting information. A number of newsrooms use tools like Slack-based newsbots to help journalists identify trending signals and social media mentions at an immense scale. It is interesting to note that with technological advancement, the traditional priority of ‘newsworthiness’ is being ruthlessly outpaced by a data-driven logic of ‘share-worthiness’.

Algorithms do not necessarily prioritise democracy, pluralism or social welfare for news stories; instead, they ask which content will generate the most clicks, shares and watch time. There are also some cases where the news media have started practicing automated journalism. For instance, The Washington Post uses an AI ‘robot reporter’, called Heliograf. Twana Nasih Ahmed and colleagues describe these phenomena as the ‘Click, Code, and Consequences’ framework, where the ‘Click’ economy pressures reporting and the ‘Code’ of AI-driven automation create new ethical dilemmas.

As algorithms gain influence, the role of the editor has also evolved. Their responsibilities extend beyond traditional editorial judgment to include Search Engine Optimisation (SEO), data-driven content decisions and headline optimisation. Hagar and Diakopoulos , in their 2019 article Optimizing Content with A/B Headline Testing: Changing Newsroom Practices, note that many news organisations use A/B headline testing to compare multiple headline versions and identify which performs best with algorithms and audiences.

Likewise, the distribution of news has transitioned from a centralised broadcasting model to a decentralised ‘datacasting’ paradigm. In this environment, the flow of content is determined entirely by algorithmic suggestions and data patterns rather than a broadcaster’s editorial control. This shift has created profound platform dependency. A 2024 Reuters Institute report found that the majority of people across 47 global markets get their news primarily via social media and search engines, with only one-fifth starting their journey on a news website or app.

The algorithmic era has also radically transformed the news consumption pattern.
